text.tspan: A visit to the workroom traces the life of wool,
from rest and cut to repair and reuse.

g.text: Why a useful bag should soften.
At the cutting table with Elena.
A field note on mineral glaze.
Morning light in the pattern room.

text.tspan: Before a pattern touches the cloth, the cloth is
allowed to settle. It arrives tightly rolled, carrying
the memory of storage and transit.
Unfurled overnight, its weight returns slowly and
the grain finds its natural line. At the atelier,
slowness is a practical condition for accuracy.
A hurried cut produces tension that only becomes
visible after wear. Rested cloth shows where it
The finished coat carries none of this preparation
visibly. Its ease appears simple because complexity
has been resolved upstream, at the cutting table.
What remains is the relation between body, material
and the quiet space held between them.
